When a family had a field too large to work alone, the neighbors came. Each brought a skill, one person kept the rhythm, and the work was finished by nightfall.

The firm runs the same way. Most problems aren't one problem. A stalled renovation is also a permit issue, a money issue and a paperwork issue. You get one advisor who understands every part, brings in the right licensed people, and keeps everyone moving in the same direction.

Selected work

The work, specifically.

Two recent matters, described without identifying details.

Property · In progress

The house the last contractor left

Property
Pre-1940s multi-family, Worcester County
Situation
An unlicensed contractor removed structural attic ties under an open permit. The town issued a stop-work order and the meter was pulled.
  1. Field-measured the attic structure and documented existing conditions.
  2. Engaged a licensed engineer for a stamped report the inspector would accept.
  3. Brought in licensed electricians and settled code questions before any work.
  4. Kept the unaffected unit moving so the owner didn't lose the whole building.

Questions

Before you call.

Do you perform construction work yourself?

The firm manages and coordinates. Any work requiring a license is performed by licensed, insured trades that are vetted and scheduled on your behalf.

How are fees set?

Fees are fixed and quoted in writing after intake. For credit work, nothing is charged until the work is performed, and you have the right to cancel within three business days.

Can a return that's already filed be fixed?

Usually. Most amended returns can be filed within three years of the original due date. Bring the filed return and any IRS letters.

Do you work with Haitian families?

Yes. Many clients are Haitian families in Worcester County, and the firm is comfortable working with English- and Creole-speaking households.

What area do you serve?

In person across Clinton and surrounding Worcester County towns. Tax, credit, records and digital work can be handled remotely anywhere in Massachusetts.
